review_scope: Read only the actual capture-only prompts, acquisition-status file and shared sufficiency instructions. No acquisition raw responses/answers, formal gate outputs or formal generated answers were read. Source-pilot H labels were not transferred.

rubric.complete_sufficient: All requested subquestions can be answered from explicitly stated visible facts or their direct combination, without outside knowledge.
rubric.partial_evidence: A nontrivial part of a requested behavior is explicitly stated, but at least one required detail remains missing. A clear assertive heading can support only its literal limited proposition, never unshown implementation detail.
rubric.no_answer_evidence: No requested subanswer is established. Broad topical prose, match counts, keywords and descriptive section labels may identify where an answer could be found but do not supply it. Context-only assertions can be acknowledged without being credited as requested-subanswer utility.
rubric.acquisition_failure: Operational capture failure prevents semantic evaluation; keep the row and error, but do not credit a fallback defer as correct classification.
rubric.strict_gate: allow only for complete_sufficient; defer for the two insufficient-evidence classes. Acquisition failure also defers operationally but is excluded from semantic accuracy.
rubric.partial_answer_utility: A useful partial answer may state only the listed supported_subanswers, disclose their heading-only limits, and explicitly identify missing requested details. Naming relevant sections alone is not a supported subanswer. A full answer that adds absent details is unsupported even if it happens to match an unseen source.
rubric.query_is_not_evidence: Question wording and its premises do not prove the requested facts. Retrieval entity counts/relevance percentages do not establish answerability.

limits: There are zero complete_sufficient cases in this capture. False-deferral rate and useful complete answers lost to a strict gate cannot be estimated; their denominator is zero.

All 12 semantically assessable cases require strict defer. This capture can compare inappropriate full answering, bounded partial utility and existing-generator refusal behavior, but cannot establish a balanced answerability classifier or a benefit over always deferring.
